title: Count All-Ones Squares
statement:
You get a grid of 0s and 1s. Count every square block of cells (of any size, aligned with the grid) that contains only 1s.

Squares that overlap, or that sit inside bigger squares, all count separately.

examples.why: Five single cells. Both 2×2 blocks contain the 0, so neither counts.
9 of size 1, 4 of size 2 and 1 of size 3. Counting only the largest square would give 1.

hints: Count squares by their bottom-right corner. If the largest all-ones square ending at a cell has side k, how many squares end at that cell?
Exactly k: the squares of side 1, 2, …, k with that same corner. So the answer is the sum, over all cells, of the largest side ending there.
The largest side at (r, c), when the cell is 1, is 1 + min(side above, side to the left, side up-left). A square can only grow as far as its weakest neighbour allows.

explain.intuition:
Let side[r][c] be the side of the largest all-ones square whose bottom-right corner is (r, c). Every smaller square with the same corner is also all ones, so that cell is the corner of exactly side[r][c] squares. Summing side over the grid counts each square exactly once, by its corner.

A square of side k ending at (r, c) needs squares of side k − 1 ending just above, just left and diagonally up-left. The three overlap to cover the whole block. So side[r][c] = 1 + min(up, left, upLeft) for a 1 cell, and 0 for a 0 cell.
steps: Create side with the same shape as the grid (or reuse one row).
For each cell in row-major order: if it is 0, its side is 0.
Otherwise its side is 1 on the top row or left column, and 1 + min(up, left, upLeft) elsewhere.
Add every side to the total and return it.
pitfalls: Taking the min of only up and left. A 0 at the up-left diagonal would be missed, as in [[0, 1], [1, 1]].
Counting only the largest square per corner instead of all side sizes.
Summing side values as squares of sizes (side²) instead of counting them.

complexity.space: O(rows · cols), or O(cols) with one row

solutions.title: Check every square directly
solutions.idea: For each top-left cell, grow the square one size at a time and check the new row and column for zeros; stop at the first zero.

solutions.title: Largest square ending at each cell
solutions.idea: side = 1 + min(up, left, upLeft) for a 1 cell. Each cell is the corner of exactly side squares, so add them all.

followups: Return the side of the largest all-ones square instead of the count.
Count all-ones rectangles of any shape. Why does the same trick not work, and what does?
